summary: CosmoChecker is an integrated crew health monitoring and tracking system designed for astronauts on long-duration space missions. It provides a standardized framework for tracking key physiological and psychological health markers based on established NASA Human Research Program (HRP) hazards. The platform allows crew members to perform regular health self-assessments across multiple categories—such as cardiovascular, musculoskeletal, cognitive, and mental health—enabling proactive management of health risks. By centralizing symptom logs, biometric data, and mission-critical protocols, CosmoChecker addresses the challenge of autonomous health management in space, where real-time support from Earth may be delayed or unavailable. This tool is vital for ensuring astronaut well-being during transit to Mars and long-term exploration missions by identifying adverse trends before they escalate.
details:
CosmoChecker operates as a digital health assistant for space crews, guiding them through scheduled check-ins across diverse areas of health. Each module provides specific monitoring instructions and criteria for reporting concerns to flight surgeons, effectively bridging the gap between complex research guidelines and operational daily use.

Key functions include:

  • Guided Health Monitoring: Standardizes tracking of symptoms and biometrics, ensuring consistent, high-quality data collection through a user-friendly interface.
  • Mission-Aware Escalation: Provides clear call criteria for contacting flight surgeons based on mission-specific thresholds.
  • Support for Autonomy: Designed for missions where communication latency with Earth makes autonomous health management essential.

Development, AI Integration, and Technical Implementation: The project was developed using React, Vite, Tailwind CSS, and TypeScript, utilizing Zustand for state management and Progressive Web App (PWA) capabilities.

Our development process relied heavily on AI-assisted workflows:

  • AI-Enhanced Development: We utilized advanced AI models for rapid prototyping, writing complex UI components, and optimizing type-safe state management. AI agents played a critical role in debugging and troubleshooting, allowing us to quickly isolate and resolve logic errors within the mission simulation engine.
  • AI-Driven Predictive Modeling: Beyond development support, we integrated AI-driven predictive modeling into the application itself to analyze longitudinal health data. This allows the system to identify early-stage deviations from an individual astronaut's baseline health markers, facilitating proactive, personalized health interventions before symptoms reach critical thresholds.

The project is creative in its application of complex HRP risks to an operational context, turning research guidelines into a daily-use interface. Our team prioritized mission-specific constraints—such as varying gravity levels, radiation exposure, and limited resupply capabilities—when designing the health thresholds, ensuring the tool remains highly relevant to the realities of long-duration space flight.
